recipe: Pasta con le sarde — Sicilian sardine pasta
servesNote: 2 portions — 885 kcal / 51 g protein each at £2.15/portion, or £1.72 without the fennel. ⭐ The notably cheap one, and it does not taste it: four tins of sardines deliver more protein than a salmon fillet for a third of the money.
adaptations: ⚠️ THE HOUSE HAS ONE TIN OF SARDINES AND IT IS IN TOMATO SAUCE, NOT OIL. The recipe covers this: drain them well and use them, and you have cooked the ENNA variant instead of the Palermo one. That is a real dish, not a compromise. ⛔ But one tin is not four — this needs ~350 g drained, so it is a shop either way.

✅ THE ANCHOVIES ARE IN THE HOUSE — Tuesday bought a 50 g tin for the lamb. ⭐ Do not skip them: they appear in five of the eleven sources, they are the first thing a shortened version drops, and melted into the oil they are the whole difference between sardines-with-pasta and a sauce with a savoury floor under it.
⚠️ SULTANAS ARE DOWN TO 30 g AND THIS WANTS 40 g. Both this and the tagine and the pilaf compete for the same tub. Raisins work identically.
⚠️ NO FENNEL BULB AT ALDI — it comes and goes. Make it without; you lose the aniseed and 85p, and the recipe is costed both ways.
⚠️ SPAGHETTI: dried pasta was down to 'very little' before the shop, and Tuesday bought fusilli and tagliatelle rather than spaghetti. Fusilli will carry this sauce.

prep: Put the saffron and raisins in a mug with 4 tbsp just-boiled water. ⭐ Steep for the rest of the prep, 10 min minimum. Saffron dropped dry into a pan does almost nothing, and the raisins need this to arrive plump rather than as hard beads.

⭐ PANGRATTATO. Panko and 1 tbsp oil into a COLD wide dry pan, medium heat. Stir almost constantly until an even deep golden brown that smells like hot toast — ⚠️ the colour change happens all at once near the end, so do not walk away. Tip out immediately, salt, cool. Crumbs left in the hot pan keep cooking and turn bitter.
Same pan, still dry: toast the flaked almonds, shaking often, until patchy gold and nutty. Onto the plate with the crumbs. Wipe the pan.

steps.text: Big pan of water on, ⚠️ salted LESS heavily than you normally would. This is the one pasta dish where hard-salted water routinely tips the plate over.
If using fennel: simmer the dice in the pasta water until a piece squashes against the side of the pan, scoop out, keep the water. Traditional, and the pasta picks up the aniseed.

Heat 1½ tbsp oil plus the reserved sardine oil in the wiped pan, medium-low. Onion, blanched fennel, pinch of salt. Until completely soft, sweet and translucent with no bite left at all. ⚠️ Anything still crunchy reads as raw onion in the finished dish.

Garlic, chopped anchovies, chilli powder. ⭐ Press the anchovies against the base with the spoon until they have COMPLETELY dissolved into the oil and you can see no pieces. They will not taste of anchovy; they will taste of savoury depth.
Pour in the saffron-and-raisin liquid, raisins and all. Bubble down until the pan is slack and glossy rather than swimming.
Start the pasta, 1 minute short of al dente.
Drain the sardines onto a board. Bone-in? The spines are soft, edible and where the calcium is — leave them. ⭐ Break each sardine into two or three LARGE pieces with your fingers. Do not mash them.
Add the sardines to the pan, heat to low, fold through ONCE, and leave them to warm without further stirring.

Lift the pasta straight in with tongs plus a ladle of its water. Raise the heat and TOSS continuously — actually toss, don't stir — until the sauce clings and looks glossy, adding water a splash at a time. It should flow slowly when you tip the pan.

Off the heat: lemon zest, juice of half the lemon, half the pangrattato, half the almonds, most of the parsley. ⭐ The lemon is not decoration — acid neutralises the trimethylamine that makes tinned fish taste fishy.

Serve immediately in warm bowls with the rest of the crumbs and almonds on top, fennel fronds, pepper, a last trickle of oil. ⛔ No cheese — the breadcrumbs are the cheese. Maria's next-day lunch: reheats better than most pasta because the sauce is oil-based — a frying pan with a splash of water, not the microwave. Keep the leftover pangrattato and almonds in a separate twist of foil; stirred through and refrigerated they go soft and the whole point of them is lost.
